Synopsis:
BOJ board member Masu delivered a hawkish pre-meeting speech warning that Japan's accommodative financial conditions could force rapid rate hikes if inflation accelerates. Underlying inflation is "very close" to 2%, producer prices are at 3-year highs, and cost-push pressures from the Middle East conflict and yen weakness are broadening. A September hike is near-fully priced in, with markets expecting 1.25% next week and 1.75% by Q2 2027. Masu stressed urgency in pulling real rates out of negative territory and flagged risks of corporate investment overheating.
